P.story: A zoo advertisement showing different animals and ending on the zoo’s logo.

story.setting: A bright late morning at Ridgeview Zoo unfolds as a welcoming, animal-led visit, filmed in 16:9. The acacia paddock sits beside a curving visitor path; pale sand fills its foreground, and leafy branches frame its rear fence. Nia the giraffe, with chestnut patches, cream legs, and short ossicones, stands beside those branches. Farther along the path, the river-otter pool has a low stone bank, clear shallow water, and reeds along its back edge. Pip the otter, with dark brown fur, pale whiskers, and a long tapered tail, moves between the bank and water. Beyond the pool, the lion terrace rises above the path, with warm sandstone ledges and tall grass behind it. Kito the lion, with a tawny coat, dark mane, and amber eyes, rests on its broadest ledge. Soft golden sunlight, natural greens, and warm neutral shadows unify the film. The final card pairs a simple gold antelope mark with gold lettering on deep forest green.

clips.reference_why: This opening animal scene can be established directly without a supplied image or designed graphic.
clips.paragraph: Open wide on the acacia paddock, with its sandy foreground leading toward Nia the giraffe, with chestnut patches, cream legs, and short ossicones. Move slowly closer as Nia reaches toward a leafy branch, pulls away a mouthful, and chews. Cut to a close view of the muzzle and leaves, then widen to reveal the long neck against green foliage. The narrator says, “A little wonder can change your whole day. At Ridgeview Zoo, look up and meet a world that’s bigger, brighter, and more surprising than your screen.” End as Nia lifts its head.

clips.reference_why: This separate habitat and moment require no continuity image from the preceding clip.
clips.paragraph: Cut to a low, medium view across the river-otter pool. Pip the otter, with dark brown fur, pale whiskers, and a long tapered tail, steps from the stone bank into shallow water. Track alongside as Pip paddles past the reeds, leaving a small wake. Cut closer when Pip reaches the bank and raises its wet face toward the camera. The narrator says, “Then slow down and watch the small things: quick paws, a sudden splash, and a curious face that makes you want to stay another minute.” End on Pip’s whiskers catching the light.

clips.reference_why: The lion habitat begins a new scene that can be established without a visual reference.
clips.paragraph: Cut wide to the lion terrace, placing the sandstone ledge across the lower frame and tall grass behind it. Kito the lion, with a tawny coat, dark mane, and amber eyes, lies with its forepaws extended. Push toward a medium close-up as Kito raises its head and turns toward the sunlight. The narrator says, “Take a moment for something magnificent. Bring your favorite people, follow your curiosity, and turn an ordinary day into a story you’ll share together.” End on Kito’s calm profile, with the mane gently moving.

Draw the antelope as an elegant, minimal side-profile silhouette with two slender curved horns, clearly recognizable at small sizes. Use a friendly, highly legible serif for the zoo name. Keep the symbol and lettering balanced, with generous empty space and television-safe margins. Include no additional wording, photographs, textures, borders, or decorative elements.
clips.reference_why: No logo image was supplied, so a designed still establishes the requested green-and-gold identity, simple antelope mark, and exact zoo name.
clips.paragraph: Cut cleanly to a full-frame deep forest-green end card. A simple gold antelope mark sits centered above “Ridgeview Zoo” in large gold lettering. Keep the entire design still and crisp, with generous space around the mark and name and no competing imagery. The narrator says, “Your next great day out starts at Ridgeview Zoo. Come for the animals. Leave with a little more wonder. Plan your visit today.” Finish the voice-over before the cut to black, holding the complete logo through the final frame.
